text_en: In the one hundred sixtieth year Alexander Epiphanes, son of Antiochus, landed and occupied Ptolemais. They welcomed him, and there he began to reign.
text_cn: 一百六十年，安提约古儿子亚历山大厄丕法乃上去，占领了仆托肋买，人民欢迎他在那里为王。

text_en: When King Demetrius heard of it, he assembled a very large army and marched out to meet him in battle.
text_cn: 德默特琉王听说这事，就集合大军，去与他交战。

text_en: Demetrius sent Jonathan a letter in peaceable words to honor him;
text_cn: 同时，德默特琉致书约纳堂，言辞温和，且提高他的权位，

text_en: for he said to himself, “Let us act first to make peace with him before he makes peace with Alexander against us,
text_cn: 因为德默特琉说：“我们要赶快与他缔结和好，免得他先与亚历山大联合，反抗我们，

text_en: for he will remember all the wrongs that we did to him and to his brothers and his nation. ”
text_cn: 又恐怕他还记念我们对他的兄弟及他的百姓所行的恶事。”

text_en: So Demetrius gave him authority to recruit troops, to equip them with arms, and to become his ally; and he commanded that the hostages in the citadel should be released to him.
text_cn: 于是，便将调集军队及准备军械的权柄交给约纳堂，将他看作自己的同盟，又下令将堡垒里的人质，交还给他，

text_en: Then Jonathan came to Jerusalem and read the letter in the hearing of all the people and of those in the citadel.
text_cn: 约纳堂来到耶路撒冷，当着百姓及住在堡垒里的人面前，宣读了这封书信。

text_en: They were greatly alarmed when they heard that the king had given him authority to recruit troops.
text_cn: 堡垒里的人一听王给了他调集军队的权柄，都很害怕。

text_en: But those in the citadel released the hostages to Jonathan, and he returned them to their parents.
text_cn: 他们便将人质交还给约纳堂，约纳堂再转交给各人的父母。

text_en: And Jonathan took up residence in Jerusalem and began to rebuild and restore the city.
text_cn: 以后约纳堂住在耶路撒冷，开始重修京城，使恢复旧观。

text_en: He directed those who were doing the work to build the walls and encircle Mount Zion with squared stones, for better fortification; and they did so.
text_cn: 他命令工人，用方石修筑垣（yuán）墙和熙雍山的四周，以作防御；他们就这样作了。

text_en: Then the foreigners who were in the strongholds that Bacchides had built fled;
text_cn: 住在巴基德所修建的堡垒里的外方人，都已逃走，

text_en: all of them left their places and went back to their own lands.
text_cn: 各人都离开岗位，回到本国，

text_en: Only in Beth-zur did some remain who had forsaken the law and the commandments, for it served as a place of refuge.
text_cn: 只在贝特族尔，还留下几个背弃法律，不守诫命的人，因为那里是避难藏身的地方。

text_en: Now King Alexander heard of all the promises that Demetrius had sent to Jonathan, and he heard of the battles that Jonathan and his brothers had fought, of the brave deeds that they had done, and of the troubles that they had endured.
text_cn: 那时，亚历山大王听到德默特琉允许给的约纳堂的事，同时还有人将约纳堂及他弟兄们的作战，英勇事迹和遭遇的打击等，给他述说了，

text_en: So he said, “Shall we find another such man? Come now, we will make him our friend and ally. ”
text_cn: 就说：“难道我们还能找到这样的一个人吗？我们要使他作为我们的朋友，作我们的同盟！”

text_en: And he wrote a letter and sent it to him, in the following words:
text_cn: 遂写信给约纳堂，信上说：

text_en: “King Alexander to his brother Jonathan, greetings.
text_cn: “亚历山大王祝约纳堂兄安好！

text_en: We have heard about you, that you are a mighty warrior and worthy to be our friend.
text_cn: 听说你是英勇有为之士，适合作我们的朋友。

text_en: And so we have appointed you today to be the high priest of your nation; you are to be called the king’s Friend and you are to take our side and keep friendship with us. ” He also sent him a purple robe and a golden crown.
text_cn: 现今我委任你作你百姓的大司祭，并称你是君王的朋友，──同时给他送来紫袍和金冠──愿你关心我们的事，与我们保持友谊。”

text_en: So Jonathan put on the sacred vestments in the seventh month of the one hundred sixtieth year, at the festival of booths, and he recruited troops and equipped them with arms in abundance.
text_cn: 一百六十年七月帐棚节日， 约纳堂乃穿上圣服，调集军队，并准备了大批武器。

text_en: When Demetrius heard of these things he was distressed and said,
text_cn: 德默特琉一听说了这事，便忧闷地说：

text_en: “What is this that we have done? Alexander has gotten ahead of us in forming a friendship with the Jews to strengthen himself.
text_cn: “我们怎么竟让亚历山大在我们之先与犹太人结为友好，作为后盾？

text_en: I also will write them words of encouragement and promise them honor and gifts, so that I may have their help. ”
text_cn: 我也要用委婉的言辞，许以地位和礼品，给他们写信，诱导他们也作我的助手。”

text_en: So he sent a message to them in the following words: “King Demetrius to the nation of the Jews, greetings.
text_cn: 于是给犹太人写了以下的信说：“德默特琉王祝犹太民族安好！

text_en: Since you have kept your agreement with us and have continued your friendship with us, and have not sided with our enemies, we have heard of it and rejoiced.
text_cn: 由于你们持守以前与我们订立的条约，保持了我们之间的友谊，没有与我们的仇敌联合，我们听了很是高兴。

text_en: Now continue still to keep faith with us, and we will repay you with good for what you do for us.
text_cn: 现在，若你们继续忠于我们，你们为我们作的一切，我们必破格还报：

text_en: We will grant you many immunities and give you gifts.
text_cn: 给你们种种豁免，赠与你们各种礼品。

text_en: “I now free you and exempt all the Jews from payment of tribute and salt tax and crown levies,
text_cn: 现在豁免你们全犹太人丁税、盐税和王冠金。

text_en: and instead of collecting the third of the grain and the half of the fruit of the trees that I should receive, I release them from this day and henceforth. I will not collect them from the land of Judah or from the three districts added to it from Samaria and Galilee, from this day and for all time.
text_cn: 由犹太本地，及划归犹太的撒玛黎雅和加里肋亚的三个地区，我所得出产的三分之一和树上果实的一半，今日都一概豁免，由今日起直到永远。

text_en: Jerusalem and its environs, its tithes and its revenues, shall be holy and free from tax.
text_cn: 耶路撒冷应是圣的，所以这城及其四郊，免交什一之物和赋税。

text_en: I release also my control of the citadel in Jerusalem and give it to the high priest, so that he may station in it men of his own choice to guard it.
text_cn: 对于耶路撒冷堡垒的权利，我也放弃，让与大司祭，他可任意委任自己拣选的人，驻在那里护守。

text_en: And everyone of the Jews taken as a captive from the land of Judah into any part of my kingdom, I set free without payment; and let all officials cancel also the taxes on their livestock.
text_cn: 凡从犹太地掳至我国的犹太人，我都恢复他们的自由，毫无代价，而且还豁免他们的赋税和牲畜税。

text_en: “All the festivals and sabbaths and new moons and appointed days, and the three days before a festival and the three after a festival—let them all be days of immunity and release for all the Jews who are in my kingdom.
text_cn: 凡一切的节日、安息日、朔日、指定的庆日，以及各庆节前后三日，为住在我国内的一切犹太人，都成为享有特权与免役的日子：

text_en: No one shall have authority to exact anything from them or annoy any of them about any matter.
text_cn: 为一切事件，谁也无权干涉及骚扰他们中任何一人。

text_en: “Let Jews be enrolled in the king’s forces to the number of thirty thousand men, and let the maintenance be given them that is due to all the forces of the king.
text_cn: 可招募三万犹太人加入王家军队，所给军饷，与一切王家军队同。

text_en: Let some of them be stationed in the great strongholds of the king, and let some of them be put in positions of trust in the kingdom. Let their officers and leaders be of their own number, and let them live by their own laws, just as the king has commanded in the land of Judah.
text_cn: 从这些人中，抽调一部分，分驻在国王的主要堡垒里；再由这些人中，选拔一部分，出任国家信托的职位；还可将自己的人派作他们的官员和将领，按照自己的法律行事，正如王从前在犹太地命令过一样。

text_en: “As for the three districts that have been added to Judea from the country of Samaria, let them be annexed to Judea so that they may be considered to be under one ruler and obey no other authority than the high priest.
text_cn: 由撒玛黎雅境内，划归犹太的三区， 应与犹太合并为一，全受一人统治，除大司祭外，不应听从别人。

text_en: Ptolemais and the land adjoining it I have given as a gift to the sanctuary in Jerusalem, to meet the necessary expenses of the sanctuary.
text_cn: 我将仆托肋买及其所属，赠予耶路撒冷的圣所，其收入作为圣所需要的经费。

text_en: I also grant fifteen thousand shekels of silver yearly out of the king’s revenues from appropriate places.
text_cn: 我每年由丰富之地纳入王库的银钱，拨出一万五千‘协刻耳’。

text_en: And all the additional funds that the government officials have not paid as they did in the first years, they shall give from now on for the service of the temple.
text_cn: 凡前几年，官员们所没有缴纳的银钱，从现在起，他们都得交还，以作圣殿的经费。

text_en: Moreover, the five thousand shekels of silver that my officials have received every year from the income of the services of the temple, this too is canceled, because it belongs to the priests who minister there.
text_cn: 此外，每年由圣所的收入内，征收的五千银钱也一概豁免，因为这笔钱，应归那些尽圣职的司祭所有。

text_en: And all who take refuge at the temple in Jerusalem, or in any of its precincts, because they owe money to the king or are in debt, let them be released and receive back all their property in my kingdom.
text_cn: 凡到耶路撒冷圣殿，或殿院内逃避国债与私债的，都一律赦免；至于他在我国内的一切所有，仍归他所有。

text_en: “Let the cost of rebuilding and restoring the structures of the sanctuary be paid from the revenues of the king.
text_cn: 为建筑及修理圣所的工程，花费也由王库支付。

text_en: And let the cost of rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem and fortifying it all around, and the cost of rebuilding the walls in Judea, also be paid from the revenues of the king. ”
text_cn: 凡为修筑耶路撒冷的城墙，及其四周的堡垒，以及犹太各地的城墙，所用的经费，都由王库支付。”

text_en: When Jonathan and the people heard these words, they did not believe or accept them, because they remembered the great wrongs that Demetrius had done in Israel and how much he had oppressed them.
text_cn: 约纳堂与百姓听了这些话，既不相信，也不接受，因为都还记得：他加给以色列的一切灾难，及怎样虐待了他们。

text_en: They favored Alexander, because he had been the first to speak peaceable words to them, and they remained his allies all his days.
text_cn: 何况亚历山大首先与他们和谈，于是他们拥护他，与他永结同盟。

text_en: Now King Alexander assembled large forces and encamped opposite Demetrius.
text_cn: 那时，亚历山大王集合大军，出发攻打德默特琉。

text_en: The two kings met in battle, and the army of Demetrius fled, and Alexander pursued him and defeated them.
text_cn: 两王互相交锋，亚历山大的军队败退，德默特琉追赶，大获胜利。

text_en: He pressed the battle strongly until the sun set, and on that day Demetrius fell.
text_cn: 但亚历山大仍继续苦战，直到日落，德默特琉竟在这天阵亡。

text_en: Then Alexander sent ambassadors to Ptolemy king of Egypt with the following message:
text_cn: 亚历山大于是派遣使者，到埃及王仆托肋米前，这样说：

text_en: “Since I have returned to my kingdom and have taken my seat on the throne of my ancestors, and established my rule—for I crushed Demetrius and gained control of our country;
text_cn: “自从我回到祖国，便坐上了我祖先的宝座，我战胜德默特琉，得掌握主权，且占据我们的土地。──

text_en: I met him in battle, and he and his army were crushed by us, and we have taken our seat on the throne of his kingdom—
text_cn: 原来我与他宣战，打败他和他的军队，就坐上他的王位；──

text_en: now therefore let us establish friendship with one another; give me now your daughter as my wife, and I will become your son-in-law, and will make gifts to you and to her in keeping with your position. ”
text_cn: 现在，让我们彼此结好，请将女儿嫁给我为妻，我做你的女婿，且将相称于你的礼物，送给你和她。”

text_en: Ptolemy the king replied and said, “Happy was the day on which you returned to the land of your ancestors and took your seat on the throne of their kingdom.
text_cn: 仆托肋米王回答说：“你回归祖国，登上你祖先王位的那一天，真是个好日子！

text_en: And now I will do for you as you wrote, but meet me at Ptolemais, so that we may see one another, and I will become your father-in-law, as you have said. ”
text_cn: 如今我要按你所写的实行，可是请你亲到仆托肋买，我们好彼此会面，我要按你说的，使你作我的女婿。”

text_en: So Ptolemy set out from Egypt, he and his daughter Cleopatra, and came to Ptolemais in the one hundred sixty-second year.
text_cn: 一百六十二年，仆托肋米和他的女儿克娄帕达，离开埃及，来到仆托肋买。

text_en: King Alexander met him, and Ptolemy gave him his daughter Cleopatra in marriage, and celebrated her wedding at Ptolemais with great pomp, as kings do.
text_cn: 亚历山大王来欢迎他，他就把女儿克娄帕达给亚历山大为妻，并在仆托肋买，按王礼隆重的举行了婚礼。

text_en: Then King Alexander wrote to Jonathan to come and meet him.
text_cn: 那时，亚历山大王也给约纳堂写信，请他来与自己会面。

text_en: So he went with pomp to Ptolemais and met the two kings; he gave them and their Friends silver and gold and many gifts, and found favor with them.
text_cn: 约纳堂便堂堂正正地来到了仆托肋买，与二王会面，也给他们和他们的朋友，送来金银并许多礼品，深得他们的欢心。

text_en: A group of malcontents from Israel, renegades, gathered together against him to accuse him; but the king paid no attention to them.
text_cn: 那时，以色列有些歹徒，即违背法律人，聚集起来控告他，无如国王置之不理，

text_en: The king gave orders to take off Jonathan’s garments and to clothe him in purple, and they did so.
text_cn: 王反命人脱去约纳堂的衣服，给他穿上紫袍。人就照样作了。

text_en: The king also seated him at his side; and he said to his officers, “Go out with him into the middle of the city and proclaim that no one is to bring charges against him about any matter, and let no one annoy him for any reason. ”
text_cn: 王又叫他坐在自己身边，向官员说：“你们陪着他往城里去，宣布说：无论因为什么事，不得控告他；在一切事上，不得干扰他。”

text_en: When his accusers saw the honor that was paid him, in accord with the proclamation, and saw him clothed in purple, they all fled.
text_cn: 那时，控告他的人，一见他身披紫袍，享受的光荣如所宣布的一样，就都逃走了。

text_en: Thus the king honored him and enrolled him among his chief Friends, and made him general and governor of the province.
text_cn: 国王为光荣他，又将他列入一等朋友中，并且封他为统帅，为总督。

text_en: And Jonathan returned to Jerusalem in peace and gladness.
text_cn: 约纳堂然后平安回到耶路撒冷，非常喜欢。

text_en: In the one hundred sixty-fifth year Demetrius son of Demetrius came from Crete to the land of his ancestors.
text_cn: 一百六十五年， 德默特琉儿子德默特琉，由克里特回到祖国。

text_en: When King Alexander heard of it, he was greatly distressed and returned to Antioch.
text_cn: 亚历山大王听说这消息，很是忧愁，就回到安提约基雅去。

text_en: And Demetrius appointed Apollonius the governor of Coelesyria, and he assembled a large force and encamped against Jamnia. Then he sent the following message to the high priest Jonathan:
text_cn: 德默特琉立阿颇罗尼为切肋叙利亚的总督。阿颇罗尼遂集合大军，在雅木尼雅扎营，且派人去见大司祭约纳堂说：

text_en: “You are the only one to rise up against us, and I have fallen into ridicule and disgrace because of you. Why do you assume authority against us in the hill country?
text_cn: “只有你起来攻击我们，因为你的缘故，我为人耻笑，受人非难，你为什么在山上向我们示威呢？

text_en: If you now have confidence in your forces, come down to the plain to meet us, and let us match strength with each other there, for I have with me the power of the cities.
text_cn: 所以现在，如果你仗恃（shì）兵力，就请下到平原，到我们这里，彼此较量一下，因为我有许多城池可倚恃（shì）。

text_en: Ask and learn who I am and who the others are that are helping us. People will tell you that you cannot stand before us, for your ancestors were twice put to flight in their own land.
text_cn: 你要查询一下我是谁，其他作我们后盾又是谁。人都说，你们决不能抵抗我们，因为你的祖先，曾在自己的土地上，逃跑过两次。

text_en: And now you will not be able to withstand my cavalry and such an army in the plain, where there is no stone or pebble, or place to flee. ”
text_cn: 现在这平原里没有石头，也没有磐石，更没有逃避的地方，你决不能抵抗骑兵，和这么多的军队。”

text_en: When Jonathan heard the words of Apollonius, his spirit was aroused. He chose ten thousand men and set out from Jerusalem, and his brother Simon met him to help him.
text_cn: 约纳堂一听阿颇罗尼的这些话，勃然大怒，挑选了一万人，从耶路撒冷出发，他哥哥息孟也与他会合，给他助战。

text_en: He encamped before Joppa, but the people of the city closed its gates, for Apollonius had a garrison in Joppa.
text_cn: 他便在约培对面扎了营。城里的人关了城门，因为约培城内有阿颇罗尼的军队。犹太人于是攻城，

text_en: So they fought against it, and the people of the city became afraid and opened the gates, and Jonathan gained possession of Joppa.
text_cn: 城中人心里害怕，就开了门，约纳堂遂占领了约培。

text_en: When Apollonius heard of it, he mustered three thousand cavalry and a large army, and went to Azotus as though he were going farther. At the same time he advanced into the plain, for he had a large troop of cavalry and put confidence in it.
text_cn: 阿颇罗尼听说这事，遂即动员三千骑兵，一队庞大的步兵，假作过路的样式，向阿左托进发， 却突然开往平原，因为那里有他所依仗的一大队骑兵。

text_en: Jonathan pursued him to Azotus, and the armies engaged in battle.
text_cn: 那时，约纳堂尾随阿颇罗尼，也赶到阿左托，双方军队于是交锋，

text_en: Now Apollonius had secretly left a thousand cavalry behind them.
text_cn: 阿颇罗尼曾留下一千骑兵，在他们背后埋伏。

text_en: Jonathan learned that there was an ambush behind him, for they surrounded his army and shot arrows at his men from early morning until late afternoon.
text_cn: 约纳堂也知道自己背后有埋伏；军队遂被包围，从早到晚，受敌箭射击。

text_en: But his men stood fast, as Jonathan had commanded, and the enemy’s horses grew tired.
text_cn: 但军人遵从约纳堂的命令，坚持不动，敌人的战马终于疲乏。

text_en: Then Simon brought forward his force and engaged the phalanx in battle (for the cavalry was exhausted); they were overwhelmed by him and fled,
text_cn: 息孟于是引军队出击，加入阵线，敌军终因骑兵都已疲惫，大败逃走。

text_en: and the cavalry was dispersed in the plain. They fled to Azotus and entered Beth-dagon, the temple of their idol, for safety.
text_cn: 骑兵在平原里四散奔逃，逃到阿左托，进入他们的达贡庙逃命。

text_en: But Jonathan burned Azotus and the surrounding towns and plundered them; and the temple of Dagon, and those who had taken refuge in it, he burned with fire.
text_cn: 但是，约纳堂焚毁了阿左托及其四周村镇，得了其中的战利品，又将达贡庙和逃到里面的人，都放火烧了。

text_en: The number of those who fell by the sword, with those burned alive, came to eight thousand.
text_cn: 这次死在刀下和烧死的，约有八千人。

text_en: Then Jonathan left there and encamped against Askalon, and the people of the city came out to meet him with great pomp.
text_cn: 约纳堂离开那里，又在阿市刻隆扎营，城里的人都出来热烈地欢迎他。

text_en: He and those with him then returned to Jerusalem with a large amount of booty.
text_cn: 约纳堂然后率领部下，带着许多战利品，回了耶路撒冷。

text_en: When King Alexander heard of these things, he honored Jonathan still more;
text_cn: 亚历山大王一听说这事，就更加光荣约纳堂：

text_en: and he sent to him a golden buckle, such as it is the custom to give to the King’s Kinsmen. He also gave him Ekron and all its environs as his possession.
text_cn: 就是将按习惯应赐给君王贵戚的金扣，送给他；并且还将厄刻龙及其属地，赐给他作为产业。
